playbook:
**Playbook for ref_commons (shared fishery, private catch submissions):**

- Before my first catch, compute the total the stock can sustainably yield across all remaining seasons and boats. If the announced "sustainable share per boat" is roughly constant season to season, the stock is near its equilibrium; small overages barely hurt regeneration.
- In the first season, don't take a big speculative overage (15 was too aggressive early — it shaved the stock for little gain). Instead take roughly the sustainable share plus a small margin, since others tend to fish at or just under the sustainable level and keep the stock stable anyway.
- In middle seasons, match the top of what others are landing (visible in the harbour record), not more. The stock stays flat when all three boats sit near sustainability, so my marginal overage is nearly free profit — but keep it small (about +0.5 to +1 over the sustainable share) so the stock never trends down.
- Watch the recorded landings each season. If the other boats start fishing below the sustainable share, the stock regrows and I can take more. If the stock starts declining, drop to or below the sustainable share immediately — the collapse penalty (zero forever) dwarfs any catch gains.
- On the final season, there is no future: take as much as I possibly can, subject only to not zeroing the stock in a way that voids my own catch if the rules punish landing more than exists. I left ~8–10 fish on the table by taking only 10.5 at the end; that was my biggest mistake. If the stock is around 90 and the rules don't cap me, submit a very large number in the last season.
- Never trust other boats to be strategic defectors here; they typically play near-sustainable, so the equilibrium holds. My edge comes from the small persistent margin plus the final-season grab, not from early aggression.

1.text:
**Playbook — shared fishery**

1. When the first season opens with a healthy stock and a stated sustainable share, I submit exactly the sustainable share. Playing at the sustainable level kept the stock near 95 the whole game and there was no collapse pressure.

2. When other boats overfish slightly in early seasons (e.g. one taking 15 while others take ~10–11), I do not punish them or chase them — I keep my catch at the sustainable share. The stock absorbed their overage fine, and my restraint cost me almost nothing.

3. When the stock stays roughly flat season to season (small drift around 90–96), I keep submitting the sustainable share, adjusted down slightly each season as the stock ticks down. Do not creep upward to "stay competitive" — the small extra tenths gained nothing.

4. When I see the reported landings each season, I check whether total catch exceeded regrowth. If the stock is falling more than a couple of points a season, I cut my catch below the sustainable share to compensate; if flat, hold steady.

5. In the final season, when no future seasons remain, I submit a large catch (well above sustainable — roughly 1.5× the share) since conservation no longer has value. If stock is near 90+, a final grab of 15+ is safe and adds meaningfully to my total.

6. In the last-but-one season, I do not ramp up much — one season of restraint keeps the final-season stock high, which makes the final grab bigger.

7. Generally: my score comes almost entirely from many steady sustainable seasons plus a big last-season take. Cooperation held in this game, so I never needed to defect early. If I ever see the stock dropping fast toward collapse (say below 50), I cut to a minimal catch immediately rather than gambling on others doing the same.

2.text:
**Playbook — ref_commons**

1. When the first season opens, I submit slightly below the stated sustainable share (about 10% under). This signals restraint, keeps the stock healthy, and costs me almost nothing.

2. In all middle seasons, I take roughly the sustainable share, maybe nudged up by 0.1–0.2. The others tend to converge near the sustainable number too, so the stock stays flat around 90–95 and everyone keeps earning. I do not take large mid-game grabs — they'd trigger retaliation and shrink later shares.

3. I watch the history lines. If the other boats land more than the sustainable share, I still hold near my share rather than escalate; the stock regrows 50% of what's left, so small overages are absorbed. I only escalate if the stock is clearly collapsing anyway.

4. On the final season, there is no future to protect. I take a large catch — roughly 1.5x the sustainable share or whatever the remaining stock clearly supports — because the last-round incentive dominates and others are likely also defecting.

5. Overall shape: cooperate at ~sustainable for every season except the last, then defect hard on the last. Total take lands around 65–70 out of a cooperative baseline of ~60, without ever risking a collapse that zeroes everyone.

6. What did not work / to avoid: nothing failed here, but I should not over-restrain. Taking 10 when the share was 11.1 in the opening round bought no visible goodwill from the other boats — they took 15 and 11 anyway. Open at most a token amount under the share, not a full unit.
